eyebrow: What a catalog entity actually captures

steps.label: kind: Component
steps.sub: the entity type -- Component, API, Resource, System, Group, or User

steps.label: owner: group:payments-team
steps.sub: a real team, not a name nobody can reach

steps.label: dependsOn: [...]
steps.sub: builds the org-wide dependency graph automatically

code:
apiVersion: backstage.io/v1alpha1
kind: Component
metadata:
  name: checkout-service
  description: Handles cart checkout and payment capture
  tags: [payments, tier-1]
spec:
  type: service
  lifecycle: production
  owner: group:payments-team
  dependsOn:
    - resource:default/checkout-db
    - component:default/inventory-service
caption: This one file is what makes the service real and searchable to the catalog.

code:
steps:
  - id: fetch-skeleton
    action: fetch:template
    input:
      url: ./skeleton
  - id: publish
    action: publish:github
    input:
      repoUrl: github.com?repo=${{ parameters.name }}
  - id: register
    action: catalog:register
    input:
      catalogInfoPath: /catalog-info.yaml
caption: fetch, publish, then register -- the new service announces itself to the catalog on creation.
